title: Chaos Monkey
description: Chaos Monkey — Distributed Failure Laboratory (public edition). Real documented tool; god-mode caveat applies.
body: Chaos Monkey is a real, publicly documented software tool relevant to Distributed Failure Laboratory. Netflix's tool randomly terminating instances to prove resilience. In the context of the god-mode vision, it represents the current real-world state of the art for part of what "Distributed Failure Laboratory" aspires to do: Simulates outages, network partitions, overloaded services, and storage failures. Resilience testing only.. Its documented capabilities include vulnerability scanning and policy verification, and it is used in production or research settings today. Like every tool in this database, it is presented strictly as what it is: a real tool with real, verifiable behavior — not as the aspirational god-mode system itself. Per the source paste's own caveat, "god mode" here means the highest level of ambition in software capability, not unlimited computation, infallible AI, or technology that has already been demonstrated. The accompanying demonstration program simulates the god-mode tool's pipeline stages deterministically and was executed in Node.js; its output is stored verbatim.
